title: Flat scalar comparison is the evaluation-normalized resolution roof
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe and $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of commutative ring sheaves whose ordinary scalar extension $E=S\otimes_R-$ is exact. Use module derived categories, K-flat tensor and normalized derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes in $D(R)$ and $U:D(S)\to D(R)$ for termwise restriction of scalars along $\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat $R$-complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] and $C$ any $R$-complex. In the strict models [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models] [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-roof], put $J=I_R(C)$, $B=\mathcal Hom_R(P,J)$, $F(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(P,I_R(M))$, $a_S:S\otimes_R B\to F(S\otimes_R J)$ and $v_S=F(S\otimes_R\eta_C)$. Then $v_S$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Let $c:E^{\mathbf L}H_R(QP,QC)\to H_S(E^{\mathbf L}QP,E^{\mathbf L}QC)$ be the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, and let $\Theta$ be the evaluation-normalized scalar-adjunction isomorphism [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. Under the canonical exact-extension representative identifications, $\Theta\,U(c)=[v_S]^{-1}[a_S]$. Equivalently $[v_S]\,\Theta\,U(c)=[a_S]$, with $[\ ]$ denoting localization. This equality is natural in both derived inputs and in compatible maps of coefficient rings; it requires neither finite freeness, filtered continuity nor boundedness.

proof.text: Exact-functor cohomology shows that $E$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms; the exact-derived-functor theorem makes termwise $E$ a left derived functor of itself, so uniqueness of left derived functors identifies the derived scalar extension $E^{\mathbf L}$ canonically with it: $E^{\mathbf L}QM\cong Q(EM)$ for every complex $M$. Set $e=E\eta_C:EC\to EJ$. It is a quasi-isomorphism. The natural augmentation equation $I_R(e)\eta_{EC}=\eta_{EJ}e$ and two-out-of-three make $I_R(e)$ a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives. Hom-invariance with first map $1_P$ gives that $v_S=\mathcal Hom_R(P,I_R(e))$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its localization represents $H_R(QP,[e])$.

proof.text: Apply the strict-numerator transpose lemma with the restricted regular module $T=US$. It gives $h((s\otimes f)\otimes p)=s\otimes f(p)$, transpose $[a_S]=[h]$, and evaluation into $QC$ as $[\eta_C]^{-1}[\operatorname{ev}_J]$. Apply the flat scalar evaluation model with $D=B$ and $b=1_B$. Its descent clause handles this possibly non-K-flat Hom complex. Naturality in the target along $[\eta_C]^{-1}$ and the evaluation equation of $\Theta$ then give the transpose of $d=\Theta U(c)$ as $[e]^{-1}[h]$.

proof.text: By naturality of closed transposition, the transpose of $[v_S]d$ is $[e][e]^{-1}[h]=[h]$, the transpose of $[a_S]$ in step 2. The adjunction Hom-bijection is injective, hence $[v_S]\Theta U(c)=[a_S]$. Invert $[v_S]$ using step 1 to obtain the roof identity. The evaluation normalization of $\Theta$ makes it natural in both inputs and compatible with coefficient maps; the two new lemmas give naturality of the numerator evaluation and of the scalar comparison, on representatives, inverse quasi-isomorphisms and coefficient compositions. The fixed augmentation is natural, so the denominator squares also commute. Composition, inversion and these canonical identifications preserve the squares; consequently the displayed roof identity is natural in both derived inputs and in compatible coefficient maps. None of the cited statements assumes finite freeness, continuity or boundedness.
